title: The By route counts are blank in v2 and v3 although the sheet says they are calculated
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v2.xlsx
section: v3 sheet By route, cells A5 to E10; v2 sheet By route, cells A5 to E10
description: The By route sheet carries the line 'Calculated from the Interfaces tab.' and six rows (COLLINS, File, Direct through ACE, Through partners, Not at all today and Total) with four count columns (In, Out, Both, Total), but every count cell is empty in v2 and in v3. The 36 rows of the Interfaces sheet carry the route and the direction of each interface, so the counts can be calculated without adding a value that no source gives. Without them a reader cannot check how many interfaces run in, out or both ways per route, and the statement in the Interfaces description that ACE ingests every inbound source cannot be checked either.
evidence: v3 sheet By route, row 2: 'Calculated from the Interfaces tab.'; rows 5 to 10: 'COLLINS' with every count cell empty, then 'File', 'Direct through ACE', 'Through partners', 'Not at all today' and 'Total', each with the same four empty cells. v2 sheet By route: the same six rows and the same empty cells.
proposed: Calculate the counts from the Interfaces sheet and keep the calculation rule on the sheet (done in v4: 20 In, 12 Out, 4 Both, 36 Total); the owner confirms the route vocabulary, which the Key sheet already defines, at the next review.

title: The data lake row and INT-19 and INT-20 are kept while Architecture v5 removes them
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: v3 sheet Disposition, row 'Data lake and Power BI'; v3 sheet Interfaces, rows INT-19 and INT-20; Architecture v5 slides 2, 7, 9 and 37; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17
description: Version 3 keeps the system 'Data lake and Power BI' with disposition 'Keep and feed' and the interfaces INT-19 (case, queue, decision and outcome data for reporting, out, file, daily) and INT-20 (decisions and outcomes to COLLINS for model learning, out, daily batch to the data lake), both owned by the Workbench. Architecture v5 removes the data lake: slide 2 notes 'Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19/INT-20 are removed', slide 7 says 'No data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed)', slide 9 says the data lake and Power BI are not connected, and slide 37 lists the data lake and Power BI feed among the parts that go. DP-17 and ADR-018 replace the feed with a read model in rwb-reporting built from events and call for a gap where a story needs lake data. This work package keeps every section, ID and row of the source, so the three rows stay with their v3 wording and carry P9 rwb-reporting as the owning service; the build story for them is not raised.
evidence: v3 sheet Disposition: 'Data lake and Power BI | Bank reporting | Keep and feed | Not applicable | Workbench | Receives case, queue, decision and outcome data daily | E1 | INT-19 | None'. v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-19 | Data lake and Power BI | ... | Out | File | Daily batch | Daily | DP03, DP12 | Not applicable | Workbench | E1 | File specification | None' and 'INT-20 | COLLINS | ... | Out | File | Daily batch to the data lake | Daily | DP12 | Not applicable | Workbench | E2 | File specification | None'. Architecture v5 slide 2 note, slide 7, slide 9 and slide 37. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting; none; gap if the story needs lake data'.
proposed: Keep the three rows in this inventory and record them as removed from build. If the business needs a reporting output, raise it as a new interface with a free ID against rwb-reporting when the reporting read model is specified; serve model learning from the decision records on rwb.decision-record.v1 (P7) if it is still needed, as the Temporal and Drools design describes.

title: Four services own no row of the disposition or the interface inventory
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: v3 sheets Disposition and Interfaces, all rows; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 and 45
description: With the Service column filled, P3 rwb-case, S1 rwb-valuation, S2 rwb-treatment and S7 rwb-writeoff own no row of either sheet, although each has a contract of its own in Architecture v5. The reason is the shape of the source: it inventories the systems and the interfaces around recovery, and these four services consume those paths through P1 rwb-source-data and P2 rwb-integration instead of owning one. The inventory therefore reads as complete for the paths but not for the consumers, and a reader cannot see from it which service uses the write-off postings of INT-16 or the credit decision of INT-35.
evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces row INT-16: 'GL | Write-off postings | In | File | ACE ingests the file | Monthly | DP13', owner ACE team; Architecture v5 slide 20 gives rwb-writeoff 'REST Source data: GL outcome'. v3 row INT-35 reads the NLEADS credit decision through v_ace_credit_decision; Architecture v5 slide 18 gives rwb-treatment the credit pack and the restructure calculator through rwb-integration. Slide 45: 'Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views ... Everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity'.
proposed: Record the consumer of each path on the Service rules sheet when the Service Contract Catalog is next revised; no row is added here, because the inventory counts systems and interfaces and not consumers.

title: No source names an owning service for any system or interface
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: v3 sheets Disposition and Interfaces, column Owner; Ownership Map v1, all sheets; Architecture v5 slides 13 to 20 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5
description: The Service column that the realignment asks for has no source value. Version 3 gives an Owner of 'ACE team', 'Workbench' or 'Bank platform' on every row and names no service anywhere in the workbook; the Ownership Map v1 owns tables, endpoints, events and jobs and has no system or interface sheet. The owning service of each row is therefore derived from the scope of the 19 services in Architecture v5 and from ADR-010, and the derivation is written on the new Service rules sheet, one rule per path group (SR-01 to SR-19), so each filled cell can be traced to a slide, an ADR or an Ownership Map ruling.
evidence: v3 sheet Disposition column E reads 'ACE team', 'Workbench' or 'Bank platform' on all 25 rows; v3 sheet Interfaces column J reads the same three values on all 36 rows. Ownership Map v1 sheets: Read me, Services, Tables, FK cuts, Endpoints (and the event, job and workflow sheets) - no system and no interface. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the data ownership per service.
proposed: Confirm the 19 rules on the Service rules sheet with the architecture owner; where a rule changes, the Service cells of the rows it covers change with it.

title: The data product of INT-06 (AAL) reads To confirm
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx
section: v3 sheet Interfaces, row INT-06, column Data product
description: INT-06 carries the data product 'To confirm' where every other interface names a DP number or 'None'. The row is the AAL feed, 'Data ACE already receives through COLLINS', and the disposition row for AAL says ACE ingests the data through COLLINS and the Workbench reads it through the account and customer views. The value is the marker of a missing answer and not a data product, so it is kept character for character and no DP number is assigned in this version.
evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-06 | AAL | Data ACE already receives through COLLINS | In | COLLINS | ACE ingests the COLLINS batch | Daily, end of day | To confirm | Yes | ACE team | E1 | File specification | DL12'. v3 sheet Disposition row AAL: 'Data ACE already receives | Keep | Yes | ACE team | ACE ingests the data through COLLINS and the Workbench reads it through the account and customer views'.
proposed: Name the data product of INT-06 from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the data product catalogue at the next revision of the interface specifications.

title: INT-33 (Legal Execution Department and courts) has no standard and two candidate services
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: v3 sheet Interfaces, row INT-33, columns Standard and Decision; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 19
description: INT-33 arrives 'Through partners', entered by the law firms in the partner portal, and its Standard and Decision cells read 'None'. The path spans two services: S4 rwb-litigation owns enforcement and court records, and S9 rwb-partner owns the partner instruction and the result the partner reports. The inventory records S4 as the owning service and keeps the partner entry on the Service rules sheet (SR-14). The standard stays 'None', because the contract of the partner gateway is specified in the partner portal design and not here.
evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-33 | Legal Execution Department and courts | Enforcement and court records | In | Through partners | Through the law firms in the partner portal | As entered | DP07 | Not applicable | Workbench | E5 | None | None'. Architecture v5 slide 8: 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'; slide 19 gives rwb-litigation legal actions, hearings, judgments and enforcement and rwb-partner the instruction and the result.
proposed: Decide whether INT-33 is a partner-result interface under S9 or an enforcement record under S4, and give it the standard of the partner gateway contract when the partner portal is built.

title: Three statements of v3 read as outdated and are kept word for word
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: v3 sheet Interfaces, description row 2; v3 sheet Disposition, description row 2; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 37
description: The Interfaces description says 'The Workbench owns its outbound files, the reporting feeds and the partner portal'; Architecture v5 has no reporting feed, and the partner portal sits behind the partner gateway in front of rwb-partner. The Disposition description says 'Supersedes v2', which was true of v3 and is not true of this version. The rest of the same sentences stays right: ACE ingests every inbound source, the Workbench owns the outbound files, and SMS, LINE and the audit logs leave through ACE paths. The rule of the run is to keep every value of the source and to change only what the realignment needs, so the three statements are unchanged and recorded here.
evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces row 2: '36 numbered interfaces with 32 systems. ACE ingests every inbound source ... The Workbench owns its outbound files, the reporting feeds and the partner portal ...'. v3 sheet Disposition row 2: '25 systems and tools that recovery uses today, what happens to each, who owns the data path and when. Supersedes v2.' Architecture v5 slide 37 removes the data lake and Power BI feed; slide 8 replaces the external gateway with the partner gateway.
proposed: Reword the two description rows at the next full revision of the inventory; the individual rows of the sheets give the owning service in the Service column meanwhile.

title: The partner portal row keeps the wording of the external gateway
source: Recovery Workbench System Disposition and Integration Inventory v3.xlsx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: v3 sheet Disposition, row 'Partner portal'; v3 sheet Interfaces, row INT-24, column Path; Architecture v5 slide 8; ADR-019
description: The disposition row for the partner portal says the screens run 'through the external gateway', and INT-24 gives the path 'Workbench screens through the external gateway' with OpenAPI 3.1. Architecture v5 slide 8 replaces the external gateway with the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) in the DMZ that fronts rwb-partner, and ADR-019 records the edge decision. The two cells are kept as written; the Service column names S9 rwb-partner, and the Service rules sheet records the gateway behind that choice.
evidence: v3 sheet Disposition 'Partner portal': 'Does not exist | New | No | Workbench | Workbench screens for law firms, auction houses and buyers through the external gateway; needs the architecture change with one to three months of lead time | E5 | INT-24, INT-25 | DL03'. v3 sheet Interfaces INT-24: 'Both | Direct through ACE | Workbench screens through the external gateway | As entered | DP06, DP07, DP08'. Architecture v5 slide 8: 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'.
proposed: Reword both cells to the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) at the next full revision, and confirm the direction and the standard of INT-24 against the partner gateway contract.
